Finally, you can also read a file, line by line, by iterating over its handle with a very simple

>>> fID = open("/path/to/file/words.txt", "r")
>>> for line in fID:
...     print(line)
At each loop iteration, a new line from the text file is fetched into
loop automatically stops when it reaches EOF.
: This is (possibly) the most efficient solution, especially when dealing with large text files since:
each line is read, processed and then discarded.

children.value: It is customary to close the file after processing:

>>> fID = open("/path/to/file/words.txt", "r")
>>> # do something with fID
>>> fID.close()

If you do not close the file, Python automatically close it for you when the program ends.
If you feel you may forget to close the file, use the

>>> with open("/path/to/file/words.txt", "r") as fID:
...     # do something with fID
